notes: Dates transcribed from the course syllabi. Numbered ordering is the suggested reading order.
driver: true == the underlined reading that drives class discussion.
pages marked estimated:true are educated guesses for chapter-only assignments — tap a workload number in the app to correct it.
classTime: null means the meeting time is unconfirmed; the app assumes 6:00 pm and says so. Set the real time in Settings, or fill it in here as "18:00".
Each session may carry "mode": "in-person" | "online" | "hybrid" once the in-person/online schedule is known.

material: names the physical thing a reading lives in, when that differs from "source" — so a book assigned four times is attached once. A chapter photocopied out of a collection is its own thing, not the collection: the three Christian Dogmatics chapters are by three different authors and arrive as three separate PDFs, so each carries its own material and its own attachment.
suggest: a date the app offers for a meeting you arrange yourself — inside the window the syllabus gives, one tap to accept, and overridden the moment you pick your own.

grading: per-course weights read off the syllabi. basis 'completion' means the syllabus gives credit for doing the work, so ticks drive the figure; 'performance' means only a real mark counts and the app will not guess one. watch: the things in a syllabus that cost people marks.

effortMinutes on an exam is revision time, so the planner paces it instead of letting 20% of a grade arrive as a checkbox on the day. dependsOnOthers marks work that waits on somebody else's calendar and so cannot be started in its due week.

watch: NO late work. Past the due time is a zero unless something genuinely extreme stopped you.

The Final Paper is due Thu Dec 3rd at 11:59pm — two days AFTER the last teaching class on Dec 1st, and a week before the presentation. It is easy to read the Dec 1st row and assume the paper is due in class.

Reading is 40% and self-reported in a log on Populi. Nothing is checked week to week, so the log is the grade — keep it honest and keep it current, because reconstructing a semester of it on the last day is how people lose the easiest 40 points in the course.
The Church Ministry Project needs TWO separate meetings with your pastor across the semester. It cannot be done in one sitting in December.
Papers need a word count at the bottom and go up as a PDF to Populi, in SBL style, 2nd ed.

The syllabus contradicts itself on Weekly Comments: §5.4 says every class “except the first”, but the schedule table lists Student Questions against Oct 20 as well. Six are scheduled here, matching the table. Worth one question in class so you are not short one at the end.
